items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: There was Tommy Dorsey, there was Trummy Young, there finally was J.J. Johnson, there was Jack Teagarden, there was Lawrence Brown. A thousand guys you know. So we were listening to all of them

ctx.x: The teachers. Oh yeah. They were teaching you theory and everything right from the beginning. In like in general, in the environment, you know we just had this great inspiration to try to learn how to arrange and to orchestrate. It was, a lot of it was a decision we made ourselves, we just wanted to know these things.
Sure. Who were the influences on the trombone for you back then?

There were many. At that time there were many trombone players that were very popular. Later in the fifties and sixties you started not to hear much of trombone players anymore. But in the forties and fifties there were a lot of trombone players that were popular. There was Tommy Dorsey, there was Trummy Young, there finally was J.J.
